options: A complete, isolated deployment of the platform with its own database, applications, and customizations
A single user account on the platform
A temporary preview mode with no real data
A shared database partition that all customers use together
questions.explain: Each instance is a genuinely separate deployment — data created in one instance does not exist in another unless deliberately copied or integrated.

questions.q: Why do real ServiceNow customers typically run at least three instances?
options: ServiceNow requires exactly three instances by license
So changes can be built and tested in Development and Test/QA before reaching the live Production instance employees and customers rely on
Because a single instance can only hold a limited number of records
To give each department its own copy of Incident Management
questions.explain: The Development → Test/QA → Production pattern exists so changes are validated before they reach the live environment real users depend on.

options: A report showing how many incidents were updated
A container that records configuration changes so they can be captured in one instance and committed into another
A list of software updates ServiceNow applies automatically
A type of user role
questions.explain: Update Sets are ServiceNow's traditional mechanism for deliberately promoting configuration changes between instances; this course covers them in depth later.

questions.q: What's the typical URL pattern for a ServiceNow instance?
options: https://servicenow.com/<instance-name>
https://<instance-name>.service-now.com
https://now.servicenow.net/<instance-name>
https://<instance-name>.com/now
questions.explain: Instances are addressed at https://<instance-name>.service-now.com, and the instance name itself often hints at its role (dev, test, production).

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a change built in Development doesn't just appear in Production automatically?
options: Because instances are separate deployments — promotion has to be deliberate and tracked, via mechanisms like Update Sets or Source Control/DevOps integration
Because Development instances cannot save any changes at all
Because Production instances are read-only
Because ServiceNow automatically syncs all instances every night
questions.explain: Instances don't share data or configuration automatically — moving a change between them is always a deliberate, tracked promotion step.
